note: What the black notebook says about frames, finishes, papers and supports — the specification the ledgers stop short of. Declared by hand, and every entry's pattern must be found on a transcribed page of the notebook or the build fails. The counts and the pages are read off the file.

framer.label: Frame makers, and where a frame came from
framer.note: Named on a bill, on a frame in the rack, or as the giver.

finish.label: Finishes and fittings
finish.note: Her words for what a frame looked like, and the model numbers on the bills.

paper.label: Paper, board and mats
paper.note: By the sheet and the half sheet, and by the pound where she priced it.

support.label: Panels and canvas
support.note: What was painted on, where the notebook names it.

recipe.label: A recipe
recipe.note: The one instruction for making anything, in a book of lists.

entries.means: A New York frame maker, written three ways on three pages and named again on the last frames list in the notebook: a 25 x 30 « goldish + white » at 11.50, a « grey white frame » on San Estoban, and a 29 x 36 whose sight is 27 3/4 x 34 3/4.

The frame maker of La Porte, Indiana. She copied two of its bills: four frames of February 1958 with their model numbers, sizes, finish codes and prices, and twenty-seven frames of June 1961 listed by size against the pictures they went on.
entries.note: « Ravel » twice, for the same firm's model 214.

entries.means: Frames « fancy French » and « French Elaborate », one of them of 1948 on San Estoban; also where she priced water colour paper by the pound.
Three 20 x 24 frames, « grey - antique », for the Cape bedroom, the obituary flowers and the petunias.
A 25 x 30 of May 1953, « gold, pinkish », at $18.

entries.written: Matt · made by Matt - E. 54" St.
entries.means: The new frames of 1952. The 25 x 30 « was aluminum + gold + no good on anything. Too raw sienna - awful in north light » — the one verdict on a frame in the notebook.
One frame, 22 x 38.
« ancient », « white, soft trim », on Dauphinée House of Truro, 20 x 28.
Frames that came from Mrs. Fitzgerald of Nyack rather than from a shop: one of 51 1/2 x 35, and an old one of 30 3/4 x 41 1/2 kept at Marion's.

entries.written: Hartman frame · Bertram H. · c̄ B. Hartman
entries.means: Bertram Hartman, painter and neighbour: a frame of his at 17 1/2 x 24 1/2 « not large enough », frames made for him in 1952, and the recipe below for finishing plain wood, taken down with him.
Frames that came from Edward Hopper's dealer: a silver one on Hills and Pond, 37 1/2 x 23 1/4, and two gold at 28 1/4 x 36 1/2.
On the oldest frame of page 122's list, « Old - heavy gold (glass) », 15 1/2 x 18 3/8 with a deep rabbet: the gallery's name, and nothing else about it.
One frame, 16 x 20, on Margaret VanEpps; Max Kuehne, painter, was a neighbour and a guest on the same leaves.
« in rack - 38 x 48, heavy with insert »: a profile, not a maker, and the largest frame she lists.

entries.written: gold · goldish · gold insert · white + gold · grey gold
entries.means: The commonest word on any frame line, and the finish of nearly every frame that came from the Rehn Gallery.

entries.written: Silver frame · Old Silver · silver on band
entries.means: Silver on the Rehn Gallery frame and on the Back of Cape Houses frame; « a wide streak of silver on band » on the Judson Tower frame, tarnished by 1961.

entries.written: whitish · whiterish · grey white · white + gold · white met. + gold edge
entries.means: Her word for the pale frames of the 1950s: on the Truro church, on the Revel frames of 1961, and down page 122's list.
entries.match: whit(ish|erish)\b|white \+ gold|white and gold|white met\.|grey white|white insert|white frames|white, soft trim

entries.means: On Chop Suey, 32 x 38 — Edward Hopper's canvas, in the frames list of page 122.
The slip inside a frame that takes up the difference between frame and canvas: « insert of 1 1/2" - so could be used on larger canvas », « 1950 - insert removed to fit 29 x 36 ».
Burges-Revel's models, by number: 200 with an insert for the 29 x 36 and 25 x 30, 214 for the 22 x 32 and 20 x 28, 241 in « 819 beige » for the Pochards.
Whatman water colour paper, by the half sheet: « 1/2 sheet Watmans = 22 1/2 x 15 1/2 », « Watman" 1/2 sheet - 15 x 22 ».
Mat paper from Lindenmeyr, the paper merchant: 25 x 38 the sheet, 19 x 25 the half.
Water colour paper priced by weight: 72 lb at 20¢ and 140 lb at 39¢, against Robinson's 23¢, 37¢ and 50¢ for 72, 90 and 140.

entries.written: Water color pad · Water Color pads
entries.means: 14 x 20, written on page 8 and again on page 121.
Her unit for a water colour: half of a 22 x 30 sheet, 15 x 22, or of a sheet of mat paper.

entries.written: mat · Mats 19 x 25 · Largest mat 23" x 30" · in 4" mat
entries.means: The mount a water colour sits in, with its width: « Mat 2" - bottom 2 1/2 », « Old mats - outside - 19 x 25 ».
« 1/2 sheet 20 1/2 x 31 », listed with the mat papers.
« 13 x 19 ? », with her own question mark, among the water colour sizes of page 6.

entries.written: Oil sketch box panels · Wood panels · Small oils - 10 x 14
entries.means: 10 x 14, the size of the oil sketch box and of the early Provincetown oils listed under it.

Named only for what a frame shows of it: « what shows of canvas = 21 3/4 x 37 5/8 », « Canvas 36 x more than 23 1/2 ». The ledgers state a canvas's size; the notebook states what is left of it inside a frame.

Four numbered steps taken down with B. Hartman — shellac; white liquid shoe polish; dry colour, pastel, rubbed in; wax — the one recipe for a frame in the archive, beside the paint formulae the ledgers carry for the canvases.
